analysis.one_liner: Hyundai Motor India designs, makes and sells passenger vehicles (SUVs like Creta and Venue lead the range) domestically and exports to around 85 countries, as the Indian listed arm of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company.
analysis.whats_happening: Hyundai's board meets on 28 October 2026 to approve Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) results, just four days from today. The last reported quarter, Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026), saw profit fall 35% year-on-year to ₹889 crore as EBITDA margin slipped to 9.3%, hurt by a supplier-fire-linked production loss (roughly 13,900 units) and a 19.6% drop in export volumes tied to the West Asia conflict. Separately, Tamil Nadu tax authorities raised a ₹517 crore GST demand for FY18-20 SUV sales, which the company intends to contest.
analysis.plain_terms: Hyundai India makes cars most people recognise - Creta, Venue, Verna - and for four quarters in a row its operating margin has shrunk, from 14% down to 9.3%. That's a trend, not a one-off blip, and it's happening alongside the company losing market share to Tata and Maruti. Meanwhile the stock is priced at roughly 30 times earnings, a richer multiple than market leader Maruti. The tension to watch: you're paying a premium for a 'quality' story while the last four quarters of numbers have been moving in the wrong direction.
analysis.quarters: EBITDA margin has fallen every quarter over the past year: 14.0% in Q2 FY26 (Jul-Sep 2025), 11.0% in Q3 FY26, 10.4% in Q4 FY26, and 9.3% in Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026), with PAT down from ₹1,572 crore to ₹889 crore over that span. Management attributes the latest hit to a supplier fire and export disruption from the West Asia conflict, not an accounting change, and has reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 8-10% volume growth and an 11-14% EBITDA margin band - meaning the company itself expects the current quarter to sit below its own target range. A GST rate cut (28% to 18%) on cars in 2026 also changed on-road pricing mid-year, so quarter-on-quarter revenue and average selling price comparisons around that period should be read with that tax change in mind rather than as pure demand strength.
analysis.performance_read: Since listing on 22 October 2024, the stock is up only 3.64% in total - essentially flat over two years - though that beats the Nifty (-7.65%) and peer Maruti (-3.84%), both of which fell over the same stretch. The stock has already dropped 33.5% from its all-time high of ₹2,782.73 (September 2025); there has been no split, bonus or demerger, so this fall is a genuine market reassessment of earnings and margin trends, not a corporate-action artifact. With only two years of trading history (short_history_mode), there simply isn't enough of a track record yet to judge long-run compounding - that evidence doesn't exist yet.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 30-31x trailing earnings, Hyundai trades above Maruti (~25x) and Mahindra (~17x), though below Tata Motors (~36x). The premium is explained by strong return ratios - ROE near 30%, ROCE 35-39%, a debt-free balance sheet - and a richer SUV mix than some peers. Whether that premium is deserved is a separate question from why it exists: margins have compressed for four straight quarters and market share has slipped from 13.8% to 11.6% over the same period, so the market is currently paying a growth/quality price for a business whose recent numbers haven't supported that story.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue has been uneven rather than steadily rising, and critically, profit has grown slower than revenue - margin compression means each rupee of sales is converting into less profit every quarter. Falling market share (13.8% to ~11.6%) means this is not volume-led growth; if anything, Hyundai is losing volume share while trying to hold margins through pricing and mix. A GST-driven price cut spurred stronger festive-season bookings in late 2026, but that is a tax-timing effect, not yet evidence of a structural turnaround.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk is minimal: Hyundai India is close to debt-free, with debt-to-equity around 0.056. The real concern is business risk - four consecutive quarters of margin erosion, shrinking market share, and event risk from disruptions like the supplier fire and export delays. The asset-light, low-debt model means profits should convert reasonably well into cash, but the underlying quality of the profit pool itself is what's under pressure, not the balance sheet.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Hyundai Motor Company (Korea) has held a steady 82.5% stake since listing with zero pledging - no governance red flag there. Foreign institutional holding has nearly halved since listing (7.4% down to about 3.2%), while domestic institutions - LIC, HDFC AMC, ICICI Prudential MF among them - have been buying, taking DII holding from roughly 7% to about 11.9% and absorbing the FII selling. There is no marquee individual 'star investor' on the shareholder register; this is an institution-only cap table. Separately, under SEBI's minimum public float rule, the promoter is expected to dilute a further ~7.5% stake over the coming years, which is a known future supply overhang on the stock.
strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (debt-to-equity ~0.056), freeing cash for dividends
High capital efficiency even after margin compression: ROE ~30%, ROCE 35-39%
Export momentum (July 2026 exports +31.4% YoY) and new Talegaon plant (inaugurated 14 Oct 2026, ₹11,000 crore investment) adding capacity toward 2030
Outperformed both the Nifty and peer Maruti over 3M, 6M, 1Y and since-listing periods, even though its own absolute return has been weak
watchpoints: EBITDA margin has fallen every quarter for a year: 14.0% (Q2 FY26) to 9.3% (Q1 FY27), below management's own 11-14% FY27 guidance band
Market share down from 13.8% (FY25) to ~11.6% (H1 FY27) as Tata Motors overtakes Mahindra for #2 position
₹517 crore GST demand (FY18-20 SUV sales) from Tamil Nadu authorities, currently being contested
FII holding nearly halved since listing (7.4% to 3.2%), and a further ~7.5% promoter stake sale is expected under SEBI public-float rules - a known future supply overhang
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results on 28 October 2026 - specifically whether EBITDA margin stabilises or recovers toward management's 11-14% FY27 target, or extends its four-quarter decline - will show whether the margin pressure is temporary (fire, export disruption) or structural (market share loss).
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly financials cross-checked across Screener.in, Business Standard and Upstox; the Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin figure is a rounded estimate. Valuation multiples (P/E, market cap) vary roughly 5-7% across Screener, Tickertape and Trendlyne due to timing differences, so ranges are given rather than single-point figures. Shareholding, dividend and price/return data are taken from the verified dataset supplied. News on exports, capacity, the GST demand and the management change is sourced from secondary outlets (Autocar Pro, Business Standard, Team-BHP) and could not be re-verified against primary NSE/BSE filing PDFs, which returned access errors during research.
